workerD1.cleanup: Owned Wrangler/workerd processes and acceptance sockets were absent after Ctrl-C cleanup; local D1 fixture files remain in the workspace.

observedFailuresAndCorrections: Full probes to :8787 and :8788 encountered HTTP 503 'Your Worker restarted mid-request'; those ports were proxies, not the dynamic env.DB worker. Each failure remains in durable raw evidence.

A first probe to a dynamic non-MCP control socket caused a Cap'n Proto size-limit failure. Per-socket GET /mcp and initialize probes identified the separate dynamic MCP listener and D1-owning workerd child before acceptance.
The first full D1 pass exposed a test-fixture request sending project_id through edit. The fixture now uses the existing action_project operation; production contract was unchanged.
The first pnpm check found the MCP display inventory omitted get_change_cursor and get_changes. The inventory was updated; final check passed.

The first rerun with added inverse assertions compared the entire restored Action DTO and found legitimate generated revision/updated_at changes; the corrected assertion requires an exact Undo starting state and equality of all restored fields except those generated metadata fields.

One intervening direct-listener invocation returned ECONNRESET before any scenario; the error is retained in the rerun evidence. A fresh Wrangler Worker run against the final built artifact then passed all 11 scenarios.

The final socket inventory recorded one direct MCP listener returning initialize 200, a debug socket returning 500/501, and a control socket resetting HTTP probes. The full acceptance used only the verified direct MCP listener.
limitations: Hosted D1, Sites trusted-header provenance and ChatGPT Work acceptance were not run or claimed.
No commit, push or deployment was performed.
